candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite fractions or fractional parts as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same common-denominator operation with nearly identical wording, scope, and exclusions.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number, mixed number, or nonstandard mixed number into an equivalent subtraction-ready form, such as adding a zero fractional part, normalizing a mixed number, or converting to an improper fraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02 and B.S02 match directly. C.S03 is broader because it also includes borrowing/regrouping, but it clearly contains the same normalization/rewriting concept, so it maps here as one part of a one-to-many alignment.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Carry out the subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators of like fractions and/or subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: These three skills are direct matches: each covers the actual subtraction after setup is complete and excludes preparation, regrouping, and simplification.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Borrow 1 from the whole part and convert it into fractional units when needed so the fractional subtraction can be completed without a negative fractional part.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 and B.S04 combine borrowing with simplification, while C.S03 combines borrowing with normalization. The shared cognitive concept across all three is regrouping/borrowing before or during subtraction, so C.S03 also maps here in a one-to-many way.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms and express it in an appropriate final form such as a simplified fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C.S04 isolates final simplification and expression, while A.S04 and B.S04 include this together with regrouping. The simplification component is clearly present in all three, creating another one-to-many alignment for A.S04 and B.S04.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks are highly aligned overall. All experts share concepts for common-denominator conversion, subtraction after alignment, and final simplification. The main structural difference is that Expert C separates simplification from regrouping less cleanly on the preparation side, using one skill for both normalization and borrowing, while Experts A and B combine borrowing and simplification in a single post-subtraction skill. To preserve all concepts without making consolidation decisions, one-to-many mappings were used for C.S03 and for A.S04/B.S04.
